sets.title: Data sufficiency directions
sets.contentHtml:
Directions (Data Sufficiency): Each question is followed by two statements, I and II. Decide whether the data in the statements are sufficient to answer the question, and choose:

  • A — if statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not;
  • B — if statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not;
  • C — if both statements together are sufficient, but neither alone is;
  • D — if the statements are not sufficient even together.

questions.stemHtml: A’s salary is 25% more than B’s salary. By what percentage is B’s salary less than A’s?
questions.solutionHtml:
Let B = 100, then A = 125.

B is less than A by 25, as a percentage of A: 25/125 × 100 = 20%.

25% is the trap: the base changes from B to A.

questions.stemHtml: A shopkeeper marks his goods 40% above the cost price and then allows a discount of 15% on the marked price. What is his profit percentage?
questions.solutionHtml:
Let CP = 100. Marked price = 140. Selling price = 140 × 0.85 = 119.

Profit = 19 on 100, i.e. 19%.

25% (= 40 − 15) is the common error of subtracting percentages directly.

questions.stemHtml: What is the compound interest on ₹20,000 for 3 years at 10% per annum, compounded annually?
questions.solutionHtml:
Amount = 20,000 × (1.1)³ = 20,000 × 1.331 = ₹26,620.

CI = 26,620 − 20,000 = ₹6,620.

₹6,000 is the simple interest for the same period.

questions.stemHtml: A can complete a job in 12 days and B in 18 days. They work together for 4 days, after which A leaves. In how many more days will B finish the remaining work?
questions.solutionHtml:
Combined daily work = 1/12 + 1/18 = 3/36 + 2/36 = 5/36.

Work done in 4 days = 20/36 = 5/9. Remaining = 4/9.

B alone: (4/9) ÷ (1/18) = 4/9 × 18 = 8 days.

questions.stemHtml: Two trains, 150 m and 210 m long, run on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 54 km/h and 36 km/h respectively. How long do they take to cross each other completely?
questions.solutionHtml:
Relative speed (opposite directions) = 54 + 36 = 90 km/h = 90 × 5/18 = 25 m/s.

Distance to be covered = sum of lengths = 150 + 210 = 360 m.

Time = 360 ÷ 25 = 14.4 seconds.

36 seconds results from using the speed difference (10 m/s), which applies only to trains moving in the same direction.

questions.stemHtml: A 40-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. How many litres of water must be added to make the ratio 3 : 2?
questions.solutionHtml:
Milk = 30 L, water = 10 L.

For milk : water = 3 : 2 with 30 L of milk, water must be 20 L. Water to add = 20 − 10 = 10 litres.

20 litres is the final quantity of water, not the amount added.

questions.stemHtml: The roots of the equation x² − 7x + k = 0 differ by 3. What is the value of k?
questions.solutionHtml:
Let the roots be α and β. Then α + β = 7 and α − β = 3, giving α = 5, β = 2.

k = αβ = 10.

Check: x² − 7x + 10 = (x − 5)(x − 2), roots 5 and 2, difference 3 ✓.

questions.stemHtml: How many integers x satisfy |2x − 5| < 9?
questions.solutionHtml:
|2x − 5| < 9 ⇔ −9 < 2x − 5 < 9 ⇔ −4 < 2x < 14 ⇔ −2 < x < 7.

Integers: −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 → 8.

Both endpoints −2 and 7 are excluded because the inequality is strict.

questions.stemHtml: What is the area of a triangle whose sides are 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm?
questions.solutionHtml:
Semi-perimeter s = (13 + 14 + 15)/2 = 21.

By Heron’s formula, area = √[21 × (21−13) × (21−14) × (21−15)] = √(21 × 8 × 7 × 6) = √7056 = 84 cm².

(Alternatively, the altitude to the side 14 is 12, splitting it into 5 + 9: area = ½ × 14 × 12 = 84.)

questions.stemHtml: In a circle, a chord of length 16 cm is at a distance of 6 cm from the centre. What is the length of a chord of the same circle that is 8 cm from the centre?
questions.solutionHtml:
The perpendicular from the centre bisects a chord. For the first chord: r² = 8² + 6² = 100, so r = 10 cm.

For a chord at distance 8 cm: half-length = √(10² − 8²) = √36 = 6, so the chord = 12 cm.

questions.stemHtml: In how many distinct ways can the letters of the word BANANA be arranged?
questions.solutionHtml:
BANANA has 6 letters with A repeated 3 times and N repeated 2 times.

Distinct arrangements = 6! ÷ (3! × 2!) = 720 ÷ 12 = 60.

120 divides only by 3!; 720 ignores repetition altogether.

questions.stemHtml: Two fair six-sided dice are thrown together. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers shown is a prime number?
questions.solutionHtml:
Possible prime sums: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11.

Favourable outcomes: sum 2 → 1, sum 3 → 2, sum 5 → 4, sum 7 → 6, sum 11 → 2. Total = 15.

Probability = 15/36 = 5/12.

(A common slip is to forget sum 11 or to count 9 as prime.)

questions.stemHtml: By approximately what percentage did Beta’s sales increase from Q2 to Q4?
questions.solutionHtml:
Increase = 180 − 126 = 54. Percentage increase = 54/126 × 100 ≈ 42.9%.

30.0% wrongly uses Q4 (180) as the base; 54.0% wrongly treats the absolute increase as a percentage.

questions.stemHtml: In how many stores did sales increase in every quarter compared with the previous quarter?
questions.solutionHtml:
Alpha: 120 → 135 → 150 → 165 ✓. Beta: 140 → 126 ✗ (falls in Q2). Gamma: 95 → 110 → 120 → 135 ✓. Delta: 160 → 150 ✗. Epsilon: 105 → 125 → 130 → 140 ✓.

Answer: 3 stores (Alpha, Gamma, Epsilon).

questions.stemHtml:
What is the area of rectangle ABCD?

I. The perimeter of ABCD is 34 cm.

II. The diagonal of ABCD is 13 cm and its length is 12 cm.

options.textHtml: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither alone is
Statements I and II together are not sufficient

questions.solutionHtml:
I alone: length + breadth = 17, but many pairs are possible (e.g. 12 × 5 = 60, 10 × 7 = 70). Not sufficient.

II alone: breadth = √(13² − 12²) = 5, so area = 12 × 5 = 60 cm². Sufficient.

Hence B.

questions.solutionHtml:
I alone: x = 7 or x = −7. Not sufficient.

II alone: only says x is positive. Not sufficient.

Together: x = 7. Sufficient, so the answer is C.

questions.stemHtml:
n is a positive integer. Is n divisible by 6?

I. n is divisible by 12.

II. n is divisible by 3.

options.textHtml: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither alone is
Statements I and II together are not sufficient

questions.solutionHtml:
I alone: 12 = 6 × 2, so every multiple of 12 is a multiple of 6 — the answer is a definite “yes”. Sufficient.

II alone: n = 6 gives “yes” but n = 9 gives “no”. Not sufficient.

Hence A.
